**Answer: Final vs Baseline Blood shows negligible effects.**

Reason: after DESeq-style differential expression analysis of the three tissue comparisons, the Final vs Baseline blood contrast yielded only 2.43% biologically meaningful differentially expressed genes (616/25,402; padj<0.05 AND |log2FC|>=1), which is significantly BELOW the 5% expectation of the binomial exact test (two-sided p = 3.1e-96; one-sided "greater" p = 1.0), and its DEGs have minimal effect sizes (median |log2FC| ~0.29; median log2FC = 0) — whereas the two dentate gyrus comparisons are far above the 5% chance expectation (~43% DEGs each, ~11,000 genes, median |log2FC| ~1.4; p ~ 0), i.e., large effects.

Methods: negative-binomial GLM (DESeq2-style, log link, size-factor offsets, dispersion trend + shrinkage, Wald tests) with design = tissue + Response covariate on all 90 samples (30 animals x 3 tissues); BH correction; DEG = padj<0.05 AND |log2FC|>=1; binomial exact test per comparison with p0 = 0.05, two-sided, alpha = 5%. Limitations: raw integer counts are unavailable (normalized counts rounded for the NB likelihood), the DESeq2-like pipeline was hand-implemented in Python (no R/DESeq2; magnitude cross-checked against the workbook's own DESeq output), and the meaning of the Code column remains an unconfirmed naming hypothesis.
